p:Lax528502Proofs.ConnectedDomination.so.label:
At a cut, a bounded set of named vertices covers enough crossing edges
to keep every connected solution connected. Component labels of the
remaining outside graph record how its named vertices are joined.
The RAM checks the induced connectivity constraints on an auxiliary
graph using the archive's component search, and retains minimum witnesses.

p:Lax528502Proofs.DominationAlgorithms.d.label:
The program reads the problem tag and returns a minimum witness. Each
tree table retains the best actual vertex set for each pair of sparse
neighborhood representatives on the two sides of the cut.

p:Lax528502Proofs.FeedbackProgram.solve.label:
The RAM counts surviving marked edges and components before and after
removing the marked vertices. The cut certificates preserve their relative
cycle rank. Maximizing the binary weight of retained vertices minimizes
the weight of the returned deletion set. Unit weights give the minimum
subset feedback vertex set.

p:Lax528502Proofs.FixedColoring.fixedCol.label:
Every cut profile has a representative of size at most the cut mim-width.
A state gives one such representative for each color. A fixed polynomial
number of word-RAM rounds combines compatible child states over intervals
of the branch-tree word, including the empty graph and zero colors.

p:Lax528502Proofs.OptimizationAlgorithms.label:
The program reads the problem tag and invokes the corresponding
polynomial-time word RAM with the graph, its computed decomposition,
and any weights or marked vertices supplied on the tape.

p:Lax528502Proofs.PathProgram.solve.label:
A connected graph is a path precisely when all degrees are at most 2
and some vertex has degree at most 1. Sparse representatives preserve
degrees truncated at 3 across a cut. The table maximizes the number
of selected vertices and returns their incidence vector.
